title: Agent SDK Sessions, Subagents, and Context

questions.question: Where should an agent store authoritative task completion, approvals, and external side-effect IDs?
options: In the session summary so resumption preserves completion and approval claims
In a stable system instruction listing approvals and last-known side-effect IDs
In durable external state with references loaded into context
In a structured confidence record attached to each completed operation
questions.explanation: Conversation is a working set. Durable state provides versioning, reconciliation, idempotency, and recovery across sessions or context loss.

questions.question: When is forking a session stronger than resuming it?
options: When no prior state exists and two agents need independently written plans
When the original task is complete but its session should remain available for reference
When continuing the same reconciled plan after any external-state tool call
When exploring an alternative must preserve the original branch and isolate mutations
questions.explanation: A fork preserves a common starting point while allowing isolated exploration. Resume continues one valid trajectory after external-state reconciliation.

questions.question: What does compaction solve?
options: Context size pressure while retaining a compact current working set
Revalidation of user identity and current scopes after a long pause
Durable recording of approvals and external transactions across restarts
Reconciliation of ambiguous side effects that may have completed before timeout
questions.explanation: Compaction reduces context volume. Durable state, authorization, and side-effect reconciliation remain separate system responsibilities.

questions.question: Which use is best for a pre-tool hook?
options: Choose which unresolved hypothesis deserves the next research pass
Block a write outside the declared file scope
Rewrite an explanation until a grader considers it sufficiently persuasive
Decide whether a legal clause creates material risk under the current facts
questions.explanation: Scope is a deterministic invariant that can be checked before execution. Semantic judgments belong in the model with evaluation and appropriate review.

questions.question: A timeout occurs after a refund request may have succeeded. What should happen before retry?
options: Retry immediately with the same key because identical requests are always safe
Resume with a larger model and infer completion from the session event sequence
Reconcile the idempotency key and external result to determine whether the side effect occurred
Mark the call failed locally, then issue a new refund operation identifier
questions.explanation: An unknown outcome can make a retry duplicate a high-impact action. Reconciliation establishes current truth and makes the next operation safe.

questions.question: A dependency changed materially since an agent session paused. What is the strongest continuation strategy?
options: Append all prior tool logs so the existing context can adapt without replanning
Fork from the paused session without reconciliation so the original branch is preserved
Resume the old plan but ask the agent to account for the dependency while working
Revalidate state, mark stale assumptions, and start or fork with a fresh structured plan
questions.explanation: Material external change invalidates the prior trajectory. A fresh working context built from durable current state avoids forcing stale assumptions through resume.
